Palm Hills selected balance-sheet figures on physical page 4 yield net current assets of EGP99,982,419 thousand minus EGP98,786,344 thousand = EGP1,196,075 thousand (EGP1.196075 billion). Physical page 2 reports rounded net debt of EGP4.2 billion. These are different measures: accounting working capital includes noncash assets and operational liabilities; net debt depends on the issuer's debt/cash definition. Neither is free cash available to investors.

For a developer, inventory and installments may convert over long construction and collection cycles, while customer advances create delivery obligations rather than ordinary borrowing. A thin positive current-asset cushion is a reason to inspect timing, not proof of insolvency. Counterevidence includes positive equity, EGP9.204446 billion cash/equivalents and positive historical operating cash flow; these do not establish cash availability or a runway. The EGP248 billion receivables figure includes off-balance-sheet amounts and must not simply be added to reported assets. Missing customer-advance composition, restrictions/escrow, debt maturities, contractual construction outlays, collectability, collateral and contingencies prevent a liquidation-value or cash-runway calculation. Total liabilities are not all financial debt. Decision: wait for a maturity and committed-cash bridge, retaining net current assets only as an accounting diagnostic; do not infer that EGP4.2 billion net debt is all debt due now or that receivables can fund it immediately.
